_meta.description: Status-lifecycle roster for the 5 grid orchestrator roles deployed as real OpenClaw agents on scout. Source of truth for the-grid's OpenClaw target (see agent-factory/docs/openclaw-paperclip-targets-plan.md, Session B1). Ported from ~/Guide/guide-core/agent-factory/roster.json's shape, adapted for an orchestrator-only rollout.

statusValues.planned: Designed but no build work started
statusValues.building: Template rendering / compose.py write_openclaw() output in progress (Session B2)
statusValues.testing: Deployed to ~/.openclaw and registered — Gareth testing before flipping to production (Session B3/B4)
statusValues.production: Live and bound to its Telegram surface, in regular use

_meta._note: This roster only covers the 5 OpenClaw orchestrators. It is independent of the Claude Code target's roster (compose.py's grid.yaml) and of the separate Paperclip manifest (Session A track) — no live sync between the three.

securityDefaults._comment: First-pass adaptation of Guide's ADR-022 securityDefaults for grid's orchestrator-only rollout. Session C (security review, gates Session B4) is expected to scrutinize and likely tighten this before any real deploy — not over-engineered here per the plan's own guidance.

orchestrator._comment: All 5 roles in this rollout are grid orchestrators delegating to already-wired Claude Code specialist subagents via OpenClaw's ACP mechanism, not executing specialist work themselves. One shared profile is a reasonable first pass; split per-role if Session C finds a reason to (e.g. finance-manager touching real money data vs. product-manager touching only specs).
orchestrator.vaultReadScope: ~/.the-grid/ (read-only — source of truth, not writable from a live agent)
orchestrator.rationale: Orchestrators need to read their own rendered identity + the-grid's role source, and delegate out via ACP subagents. No need for broad exec or write access outside their own workspace.

ceo-orchestrator.title: CEO
ceo-orchestrator.summary: Top-level orchestrator above the team. Turns a business goal into sequenced initiatives and bets, makes the build-vs-not call, sets guardrails and budgets, delegates to Tech Lead + Product Manager, gates releases, reviews outcomes against the goal.

telegram._note: Binding decided in Session B3/B4 — one dedicated bot per orchestrator, matching the existing coach precedent.

tech-lead.title: Tech Lead
tech-lead.summary: PRDs, architecture decisions, hands off to specialists, reviews output.

telegram._note: Binding decided in Session B3/B4 — one dedicated bot per orchestrator, matching the existing coach precedent.

finance-manager.title: Finance Manager
finance-manager.summary: Orchestrates the finance desk pipeline (sentinel -> analyst -> strategist -> risk-officer -> your approval queue -> scribe). Routes and grades escalation; never sizes a trade, never overrides the Risk Officer, never auto-approves.

telegram._note: Binding decided in Session B3/B4 — one dedicated bot per orchestrator, matching the existing coach precedent. First OpenClaw pilot role per the plan's Session B4.

finance-manager._note: Standalone top-level orchestrator, not a CEO delegate (personal desk, not a dev-team initiative) — matches the-grid's grid.yaml topology note.

growth-hacker.title: Growth Hacker
growth-hacker.summary: Acquisition and funnel experiments, analytics-driven growth. Runs disciplined, hypothesis-first experiments — one variable at a time, lets the data decide.

telegram._note: Binding decided in Session B3/B4 — one dedicated bot per orchestrator, matching the existing coach precedent.

product-manager.title: Product Manager
product-manager.summary: Converts intent into precise specs. Owns scope, acceptance criteria, PRDs, and tracer-bullet tickets. Does not architect or implement.

telegram._note: Binding decided in Session B3/B4 — one dedicated bot per orchestrator, matching the existing coach precedent.

product-manager._note: role.yaml marks orchestrator: false (no CC-skill delegates_to in grid.yaml today) but the plan explicitly includes it in the OpenClaw 5 — the OpenClaw target and the Claude Code orchestrator/specialist split are independent classifications.
